1.Heard Sri Shishir Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri G.D. Bhatt, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State.

However, learned counsel for the complainant/
informant
has not been appearing for the last some dates, therefore, on 06.05.2024 this Court has passed the stop order.

2. Today, no one has appeared on behalf of the complainant/ informant nor any request for adjournment has been made, therefore, this bail application is being decided on the basis of material available on record and on the basis of the arguments so advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant as well as the learned Additional Government Advocate for the State.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant has filed supplementary affidavit, today in the Court, enclosing therewith the evidence of the victim/ prosecutrix recorded by the learned trial court, the same is taken on record.

4. As per learned counsel for the applicant, the present applicant (Anurag Kashyap Alias Bugga) is languishing in jail since 23.04.2023 in F.I.R./Case Crime No.359 of 2023, under Sections 363,
376(3) & 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (in short POCSO Act), Police Station-Kotwali Sadar, District-Lakhimpur Kheri.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the present applicant has been falsely implicated in this case as he has not committed any offence as alleged in the prosecution story.

6. At this stage, attention has been drawn towards the evidence of the victim/ prosecutrix wherein the specific allegation has been levelled against one Shiv Poojan also but he has not been implicated for the reason best known to the complainant/ informant.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant has further submitted that the prosecution story and the allegations are different from the statement of the witnesses recorded during the course of investigation.

In her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix has stated that the present applicant had taken the prosecutrix to his home by alluring her and in his home the applicant had given some items to eat, resultant thereof, she became unconscious and thereafter he committed wrong act with her and the present applicant had taken obscene photographs and videos of the victim/ prosecutrix.
In her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix has stated that by giving threat to life by the knife the present applicant has taken the prosecutrix with him and committed rape.

The same story has been informed by the mother of the victim /
prosecutrix to the police.
However, there are apparent variations in such story if the statement of the prosecutrix is seen which has been recorded before the court.

8. Learned counsel for the applicant has further submitted that on account of some personal enmity between the family of the present applicant and the victim/ prosecutrix as has been shown in the report dated 20.04.2023 of the Sub-Inspector of Police, Police Station-Kotwali Sadar,
District-Lakhimpur Kheri (Annexure No.10), the impugned F.I.R. has been lodged.
He has further submitted that the victim/ prosecutrix has informed her age as 13 years but so as to ascertain her age no medical examination was conducted.
The present applicant is having no previous criminal history of any kind whatsoever, therefore, considering the period of incarceration which is more than one year he may be enlarged on bail.

9. Learned counsel for the applicant has also submitted that if the prosecution story so narrated in the impugned F.I.R. is taken on its face value, this is beyond his comprehension that the prosecutrix and her family members have not lodged the F.I.R. immediately after 15.08.2022 when the incident in question has taken place first time.

Therefore, there is delay of about eight months in lodging the impugned F.I.R. Though the F.I.R. has been lodged for the alleged second incident dated 17.04.2023 after the delay of five days on 22.04.2023 without explaining the reason of delay of five days.
Further, initially, the F.I.R. was not lodged under Section 376 I.P.C.

10. Per contra, Sri G.D. Bhatt, learned Additional Government Advocate has opposed the prayer for bail of the present applicant by submitting that this is a case where the prosecution story is intact from the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C.
Further, the evidence of the child so recorded by the learned trial court clearly shows that the child/prosecutrix has levelled specific allegation against the present applicant of committing rape.
He has further submitted that she had informed the court that when the incident in question had taken place firstly, at that point of time she was studying in Class-VII and was aged about 12 years.
In such evidence, she has categorically stated that whatever has been informed to the court while recording her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is correct.
She verified her photograph and signature on such statement.

11. Sri Bhatt, learned Additional Government Advocate has further submitted that so far as the submission of learned counsel for the applicant is concerned to the effect that initially the F.I.R. was lodged under Section 354-A I.P.C. only at the time of lodging the F.I.R. something fishy has been alleged by the informant regarding molestation etc. but while recording her statement before the learned trial court she has narrated the actual story, which is intact, therefore, the present applicant may not take benefit of fact that the prosecution story so narrated in the F.I.R. is different from the statement and the evidence of the child.
So far as the age of the child is concerned, the same is verifiable from her educational record.
Therefore, Sri Bhatt has submitted that this is a case where the offence of rape has been committed with the child aged about 11 years and two months (as per the educational documents).
Therefore, he has requested that this bail application may be rejected.

12. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the material available on record, since the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. as well as her evidence recorded before the learned trial court are intact wherein she has levelled specific allegation against the present applicant to commit rape with her when she was less than 12 years; I am not inclined to grant bail to the present applicant.

13. Section 35 (2) of POCSO Act categorically provides that the trial in the cases of POCSO shall be conducted and concluded with expedition preferably within a period of one year, therefore, I find it appropriate that the specific direction be issued to conclude the trial within time frame.

14. Since the evidence of the child has already been recorded and she has been examined and the evidence of her father is being recorded by the learned trial court, therefore, I find it appropriate that the direction be issued to the learned trial court to expedite the trial within a period of nine months.

15. Accordingly, the learned trial court is directed to conclude the trial within a period of nine months in terms of Section 35 (2) of POCSO Act and also taking recourse of Section 309 Cr.P.C. by fixing short dates, if possible, by fixing the dates on day-to-day basis ensuring that all the prosecution witnesses be examined with expedition.

It is further directed that if any of the Anurag Kashyap Alias Bugga vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin.Secy.Deptt. Of ... on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95307037/
3 prosecution witnesses do not cooperate in the trial proceedings, appropriate coercive steps may be taken by the learned trial court against such witnesses if those witnesses are avoiding the trial proceedings without having any cogent reason to that effect.

sentences.text: In any case, the learned trial court shall ensure to conclude the trial within the time frame as above.
16. Liberty is given to the applicant to file another bail application if the trial in question is not concluded within the time framed by this order.

17. Let a copy of this order be provided to the learned trial court through the learned District &
Sessions Judge, Lakhimpur Kheri by the Registry of this Court within three working days for its strict compliance.
18.

It is also made clear that the findings and the observations of this order, which have been given to dispose off this bail application, may not influence the learned trial court to conclude the trial inasmuch as the learned trial court shall conclude the trial independently on the basis of material/
evidence available on the record.
19. Accordingly, this bail application is rejected.
